about: The only superlatives Retrospect says about a night (spec 7.3): each with its source, the source's own words for every claim it makes, and the date the source said it. Everything else is phrased from NASA's log. An event belongs to the night that holds `at` in the listener's zone; stories carry no clock times, since the page writes `at` in the listener's zone. Each source opened and checked on 1 Oct 2026.

events.title: An annular eclipse across the US
events.story: The Moon's shadow ran from the coast of Oregon to the Texas Gulf Coast.
sourceSays: traveling from the coast of Oregon to the Texas Gulf Coast

events.title: A total solar eclipse across North America
events.story: Totality crossed Mexico, then the US from Texas to Maine, then Canada.
sourceSays: The path of the eclipse continued from Mexico, entering the United States in Texas
The eclipse entered Canada in Southern Ontario

events.title: The strongest geomagnetic storm in about 20 years
events.story: G5, the top of NOAA's scale. NOAA called it the strongest since the Halloween storms of 2003.
sourceSays: the strongest since the Halloween Solar Storms of 2003

events.title: A 150-meter asteroid, closer than the Moon
events.story: Asteroid 2024 MK passed 295,000 km from Earth, first reported only 13 days before.
sourceSays: pass our planet from a distance of only 184,000 miles (295,000 kilometers)

events.title: The strongest flare of its solar cycle, at the time
events.story: An X9.3 flare. NASA called it the largest so far in that solar cycle.
sourceSays: The X9.3 flare was the largest flare so far in the current solar cycle

events.title: The strongest flare of this solar cycle, at the time
events.story: An X9.0 flare. NOAA called it the most powerful so far in Solar Cycle 25.
sourceSays: it is the most powerful so far in Solar Cycle 25

events.title: A blood moon
events.story: A total lunar eclipse, the Moon over the Western Hemisphere.
